analysis: The only changed file is docs/developer/test.md, a developer testing guide. Its diff bumps the last-updated date (line 3). It adds a GLM5NextLogprobsTests description (head lines 117-120) and describes four OpenRouter-related tests: returnedAssistantReasoningRendersLikeReasoningContent, openRouterReasoningContentReturnRequestIsServed, capturedOpenRouterToolRequestIsServed and capturedOpenRouterToolServesAFiveStepConversation (head lines 176-184). No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache storage or deployment configuration changed. I checked T-041 (prefix cache) and the other supplied threat definitions against the added text. The text does not touch the SSD cache, HMAC lookup names, TTL, scoping or KEK behavior. It does not weaken any documented mitigation. The new test descriptions stress fail-closed behavior: a typed 400 invalid_request instead of a 500 on logprobs, with the engine continuing to serve. They also say captured fixtures are held byte for byte and hash-checked. They do not give instructions that route tests at production state. One open question for integration: the referenced tests (GLM5NextLogprobsTests, the OpenRouter replay tests) and the source behavior they claim are not in this batch. I cannot confirm they exist or that logprobs rejection behaves as documented. This is a documentation-accuracy concern, not a security regression. I found no new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption in this docs-only change.
